questions.question: In 2025, a state-of-the-art automated healthcare machine, a self-service digital health kiosk for basic testing and diagnostics, was installed at Lucknow. What is it called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Health ATM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Health ATM** refers to a self-service digital health kiosk designed to provide **basic testing and diagnostics** without the need for human intervention.
 
• In **2025**, such an advanced **automated healthcare machine** was installed in **Lucknow**, making it a significant milestone in technology-driven healthcare solutions.
 
• Health ATMs are equipped with a variety of **medical diagnostic tools** such as BP monitors, glucometers, thermometers, pulse oximeters, and ECG machines.
 
• They offer services like **basic health check-ups, instant diagnostic reports**, and consultations with doctors through telemedicine.
 
• These kiosks are particularly beneficial in areas with limited access to healthcare facilities, as they help bridge the gap between **patients and healthcare professionals**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Features of Health ATMs:**

 
 
• Health ATMs are compact and easy-to-use machines that can conduct **up to 40 different diagnostic tests**, including BMI, blood sugar, lipid profile, and hemoglobin levels.
 
• They provide **instant health reports** which can be shared with doctors for further consultation.
 
• Many Health ATMs are integrated with **telemedicine platforms**, enabling real-time virtual consultations with certified doctors.
 
• These machines are designed to operate in **rural and urban areas**, ensuring accessibility to healthcare services for a wide population.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Health ATMs:**
 
 
• They are widely used in places like **railway stations, airports, corporate offices, schools, and rural areas**.
 
• Health ATMs can act as primary healthcare points, reducing the burden on hospitals and diagnostic labs.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**
 
 
• **Med Kiosk:** While similar in concept, Med Kiosks are more focused on prescription medicine dispensing rather than diagnostics.
 
• **e-Clinic Booth:** These booths are typically used for telemedicine services but may not provide the extensive diagnostic capabilities of a Health ATM.
 
• **Health Pod:** Health Pods are emerging technologies focused more on wellness and fitness monitoring rather than comprehensive health diagnostics.
 
 
 
• **Global Use of Health ATMs:**
 
 
• Countries like **India, China, and the USA** are increasingly adopting Health ATMs to improve their healthcare systems.
 
• They are particularly popular in areas with **limited healthcare infrastructure**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advantages of Health ATMs:**

 
 
• They provide **quick and affordable health solutions** without requiring patients to visit clinics or hospitals.
 
• They are highly beneficial in **remote and underserved areas** where access to healthcare is limited.
 
• Health ATMs save time and effort by offering **instant diagnostic results** and telemedicine consultations.
 
 
 
• **Future Prospects:**
 
 
• With advancements in **AI and IoT**, Health ATMs are expected to become more efficient and offer a wider range of services.
 
• They can play a critical role in achieving **universal healthcare access** and reducing the burden on traditional healthcare facilities.

questions.question: When a large force acts on a body for a short time, then the force is called?
questions.solution:
__
 
• When a large force acts on a body for a short time, then the force is called **impulsive force.__**
 
• Impulse = force x time = change in momentum
 
• Impulse is a vector quantity.
 
• SI Unit of Impulse is Newton second (Ns).

__**Explanation:**__

Impulse

 
• When a large force works on a body for a very small time interval, it is called impulsive force.
 
• An impulsive force does not remain constant, but changes first from zero to maximum and then from maximum to zero. In such a case, we measure the total effect of force.
 
• The impulse caused by a force during a specific time interval is equal to the body's change of momentum during that time interval.
 
• Impulse, effectively, is a measure of change in momentum.
 
• The impulse of a force is a measure of the total effect of force.
 
• Impulse is a vector quantity and its direction is the same as that of force.
 
• SI unit of impulse is Newton-second or kg-m-s-1 and CGS unit is g.m/s

questions.question: A plant bearing both male and female flowers on the same specimen plant is called
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Monoecious**

__**Explanation:**__

A **monoecious plant** is a plant where both the male and female reproductive systems exist on the same plant. Monoecious plants possess some flowers that are female and others that are male. 

 
• **Bisexual: **In botanical terms, a bisexual flower is one that contains both male (stamens) and female (pistils) reproductive organs. Such flowers are capable of self-pollination, although they may also be cross-pollinated.
 
• **Dioecious: **Plants are described as dioecious when individual plants are either male or female, not both. This means a single plant will produce only male flowers or only female flowers, but not both. As a result, for reproduction to occur, both male and female plants must be present. 
 
• **Monoecious: **This term describes plants that bear both male and female flowers on the same individual plant. However, unlike bisexual flowers, the male and female flowers are separate; they can be distinctly recognized as male (pollen-producing) or female (ovule-producing). This strategy allows for the possibility of self-pollination, but cross-pollination between flowers on the same plant or with other plants increases genetic diversity. 
 
• **Monogamous: **This term is not specifically used in plant biology to describe sexual reproduction or flower arrangements. Instead, it is more commonly used in the context of social or mating behaviors in animals, where it refers to the practice of having one mate at a time or during a mating season or period.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to win a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Milkha Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Milkha Singh**, popularly known as the "Flying Sikh," was the first Indian to win a **gold medal** at the **Commonwealth Games**.
 
• He achieved this milestone in the year **1958** during the Commonwealth Games held in **Cardiff, Wales**.
 
• Milkha Singh competed in the **440 yards race** and secured the gold medal, making history for Indian athletics on an international platform.
 
• His victory was considered a breakthrough moment for Indian sports, as he was competing against some of the best athletes in the world at the time.
 
• Milkha Singh's achievement inspired generations of Indian athletes and showcased the potential of Indian sports on the global stage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Milkha Singh:**

 
 
• Born on **20 November 1929** in **Govindpura, Punjab (now in Pakistan)**.
 
• He represented India in three Olympics: **1956**, **1960**, and **1964**.
 
• Milkha Singh narrowly missed a medal in the **1960 Rome Olympics**, finishing fourth in the **400 meters** race.
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Shri**, India's fourth-highest civilian award, in recognition of his contributions to sports.
 
 
 
• **Commonwealth Games:**
 
 
• The Commonwealth Games are a multi-sport event involving athletes from the **Commonwealth of Nations**.
 
• India has been participating in the Commonwealth Games since **1934**.
 
• Milkha Singh's gold medal in **1958** was India's first-ever gold medal at these Games.
 
 
 
• **Other Indian Achievements at the Commonwealth Games:**
 
 
• India has won numerous medals since Milkha Singh's historic win, with athletes excelling in sports like **boxing, wrestling, badminton, and shooting**.
 
• Notable names include **PV Sindhu** in badminton, **Vijender Singh** in boxing, and **Saina Nehwal** in badminton.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Milkha Singh:**
 
 
• Milkha Singh's story has inspired countless athletes, and his life was depicted in the popular Bollywood movie **"Bhaag Milkha Bhaag"** (2013).
 
• He passed away on **18 June 2021** at the age of **91** due to complications from COVID-19.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Milkha Singh's Contribution to Indian Sports:**

 
 
• Milkha Singh remains one of the most iconic figures in Indian sports history.
 
• He helped elevate the status of athletics in India, inspiring investment and recognition for the sport.
 
• His determination and perseverance serve as a model for aspiring athletes.
 
 
 
• **India's Progress in Athletics:**
 
 
• Following Milkha Singh's lead, India has seen significant growth in track and field events.
 
• Notable athletes like **PT Usha**, **Neeraj Chopra**, and **Anju Bobby George** have brought further glory to Indian athletics.
 
• Neeraj Chopra's gold medal win in javelin at the **2020 Tokyo Olympics** was a landmark achievement in Indian sports.

questions.question: In windows, SHIFT, CTRL (control), and ALT (alternate) keys are called ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Modifier keys**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Modifier keys

 
 
• It is a special key on a computer keyboard that temporarily modifies the normal action of another key when pressed together.
 
• For e.g, Shift, Alt, or Ctrl keys are the modifier keys. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Special keys**

 
 
• A special key or media key is a keyboard key that performs a special function not included with the traditional 104-key keyboard.
 
• For e.g, **the first four buttons are shown to control the volume of the speakers and the computer's brightness.**
 
 
 
• **Lock keys**
 
 
• These keys are related to the lock part of a keyboard key for a distinct mode of operation, depending on the lock settings selected.
 
 
• **Number Lock:** It allows the user to type numbers by pressing the keys on the number pad, rather than having them act as up, down, left, right, page up, end, and so forth.
 
• **Capital Lock:** It is used to type the letters in uppercase by default rather than lowercase. Located at the left end of the keyboard, above the left shift key.
 
• **Scrolling Lock**: In some applications, such as spreadsheets, the lock mode is used to change the behaviour of the cursor keys to scroll the document instead of the cursor.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Window keys**
 
 
• The Windows logo key such as **win, start logo, flag, or super key.**
 
• This key became a standard key on PC keyboards.
 
• In Windows tapping the key brings up the start menu.
 
• Ctrl + Esc performs the same function, in case the keyboard lacks this key.

questions.question: Humans normally have ______ number of pairs of autosomes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**22.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Humans normally have **22 **pairs of autosomes.
 
• **An autosome** is any of the numbered chromosomes, as opposed to the sex chromosomes.
 
• All the chromosomes other than the sex hormones are autosomes.
 
 
• **Chromosomes** is a thread-like structure found in the nucleus.
 
• It becomes visible during cell division.
 
• In Humans, there are** 23 pairs of chromosomes in total (46 chromosomes)**
 
 
 
• **22 pairs of autosomes** (total 44) and **one pair of allosomes.**
 
• **An allosome is a sex chromosome** that differs in size, form, and behaviour from an autosome.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

__
 
• We actually have a total of 23 pairs of chromosomes in these cells, for a total of 46 chromosomes, **but two of those are referred to by letter rather than by number and are called sex chromosomes rather than autosomes** since they--that is the X and Y chromosome--help determine what sex, or gender, we are.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Humans have one pair of allosomes.
 
• X and Y are the one pair of sex chromosomes.
 
• These chromosomes contain genes that determine the biological sex of an organism.
 
• In the XY sex-determination system, the female-provided** ovum contributes an X chromosome.**
 
• The male-provided** sperm contributes either an X chromosome or a Y chromosome.**
 
• Thus resulting in **female (XX) or male (XY)** offspring, respectively.

questions.question: _________ is an example of intrusive igneous rock.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Granite is an example of Intrusive Igneous Rocks.__
 
• Granite is a common type of felsic intrusive igneous rock that is granular and phaneritic in texture.
 
• Granites can be predominantly white, pink, or grey in colour, depending on their mineralogy.
 
• When molten magma cools it forms Igneous Rocks. 
 
• There are two types of Igneous Rocks. They are:
 
 
• Extrusive Igneous Rock.
 
• Intrusive Igneous Rock.
 
 
 
• Extrusive Igneous Rock: When Molten Lava reaches earth crust, it cools down rapidly and becomes solid and rocks formed in this process are called Extrusive Igneous Rock. Example: Basalt
 
• Intrusive Igneous Rock: When Molten Magam cools down deep in the earth without reaching the earth surface, these types of rocks are called Intrusive Igneous Rock. Example: Granite 
 
• Granite is an igneous rock that forms when magma cools relatively slowly underground. It is usually composed primarily of the minerals quartz, feldspar, and mica. When granite is subjected to intense heat and pressure, it changes into a metamorphic rock called **gneiss.**

questions.question: Which of the following constitutional amendment act is known as 'Mini Constitution'?
questions.solution:
Forty-Second Amendment Act,1976: The most comprehensive amendment made so far to the Constitution; it is known as ‘Mini- Constitution’.It gave effect to the recommendations of Swaran Singh Committee.

1. Added three new words (i.e., socialist, secular and integrity) in the Preamble.

2. Added Fundamental Duties by the citizens (new Part IVA).

3. Made the president bound by the advice of the cabinet.

4. Provided for administrative tribunals and tribunals for other matters (Added Part XIV-A).

5. Froze the seats in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies on the basis of 1971 census till 2001.

6. Made the constitutional amendments beyond judicial scrutiny.

7. Curtailed the power of judicial review and writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and high courts.

• India falls under the “Moderate” hunger category.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1: **India is ranked 102nd out of 123 countries in the Global Hunger Index 2025. This statement is correct.
 
• Statement 2: This statement is incorrect, because according to recent Global Hunger Index reports, India falls under the “Serious” hunger category, not Moderate.
 
• The **Global Hunger Index (GHI)** is a tool that measures and tracks hunger globally, regionally, and by country. It calculates hunger levels based on four indicators: **undernourishment, child wasting, child stunting, and child mortality.**
 
• The GHI rankings are published annually, and India's performance has been closely observed due to its large population and persistent challenges in nutrition and food security.
 
• *Hence, both statements provided in the question are incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Global Hunger Index:**

 
 
• The GHI is jointly published by **Concern Worldwide** and **Welthungerhilfe**, two organizations working towards ending global hunger.
 
• The index uses four indicators to calculate hunger levels: **undernourishment, child wasting (low weight for height), child stunting (low height for age), and child mortality.**
 
• The GHI categorizes countries into five levels of hunger: **low, moderate, serious, alarming, and extremely alarming.**
 
• India has consistently ranked in the "Serious" category in recent years, highlighting ongoing challenges in addressing malnutrition, food insecurity, and child health.
 
 
 
• **Key Indicators of Hunger:**
 
 
• **Undernourishment:** Refers to the insufficient caloric intake of a population.
 
• **Child Wasting:** Indicates acute malnutrition where children are underweight for their height.
 
• **Child Stunting:** Represents chronic malnutrition where children are shorter than expected for their age.
 
• **Child Mortality:** Refers to deaths of children under five years, often linked to malnutrition and poor health services.
 
 
 
• **Efforts to Address Hunger in India:**
 
 
• The Government of India has implemented several schemes to address hunger and malnutrition, such as the **Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS), Mid-Day Meal Scheme, and Poshan Abhiyaan.**
 
• The **National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013** aims to provide subsidized food grains to approximately 67% of India's population.
 
• Despite these efforts, challenges persist in implementation and coverage, necessitating further improvements.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Hunger Index Thresholds:**

 
 
• A score below 9.9 is categorized as "low hunger," while scores between 10 and 19.9 are "moderate hunger."
 
• Scores between 20 and 34.9 are "serious hunger," 35 to 49.9 are "alarming hunger," and above 50 are "extremely alarming hunger."
 
• India’s recent GHI scores place it firmly in the "serious" category.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Addressing Hunger:**
 
 
• Poverty, lack of education, and inadequate health services contribute to persistent hunger in India.
 
• Natural disasters, climate change, and economic challenges further exacerbate food insecurity.
 
• Targeted policies and efficient implementation are crucial to reduce hunger and malnutrition across the country.

questions.question: According to the 'Law of Demand', when there is an increase in the price of a commodity, the quantity demanded ________.
questions.solution:
​The right answer is **de__creases__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The law of demand states that there is an inverse relationship between the price of a good and the quantity demanded of that good.
 
• In other words, as the price of a good increases, the quantity demanded of that good decreases. And conversely, as the price of a good decreases, the quantity demanded of that good increases.
 
• So, when there is an increase in the demand for a commodity, the price of that commodity will also increase. This is because the higher demand will create a shortage of the commodity, which will drive up the price.
 
• The law of demand states that other factors being constant (ceteris paribus), price, and quantity demand of any good and service are inversely related to each other.
 
• **When the price of a product increases, the demand for the same product will fall.**
 
• In other words, it can be said as **the higher the price, the lower the quantity demanded.**
 
• This occurs** because of diminishing marginal utility.**

• UNESCO is responsible for monitoring progress toward **SDG 4** of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, which focuses on education.

• **Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4):**

• **Reports and Indices by Other Organizations:**

• **UNDP:** Produces the **Human Development Report**, which includes the **Human Development Index (HDI)**, analyzing education, health, and standard of living. 

• **World Bank:** Publishes reports like the **World Development Report**, which also covers education and economic development. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **CD** stands for **Compact Disc**, which is a digital optical disc storage format.
 
• It was originally developed by **Philips** and **Sony** in 1982 for storing and playing music.
 
• Compact Discs are used for storing various types of digital data, including **audio, video, and software programs**.

• **CD-RW**: Rewritable discs that allow data to be erased and rewritten multiple times.

• Data is stored in the form of microscopic pits and lands on the reflective surface of the disc.
